nodes.name: Hydrothermal growth
nodes.procedure: Hydrothermal growth of MnCo—OH nanorod arrays on carbon paper substrate.

nodes.name: Magnetron sputtering core-shell
nodes.procedure: Magnetron sputtering of Co₃N layers onto hydrothermally grown MnCo—OH nanorod arrays (which become MnCo—CH) on CP substrate to form MnCo—CH@Co₃N heterostructures.
nodes.source_text: The MnCo—CH@Co₃N pre-catalyst was synthesized by magnetron sputtering of Co₃N layers onto hydrothermally grown MnCo—OH nanorod arrays (Figure 1a)

nodes.characterization_summary: MnCo—CH@Co₃N shows nanowire array morphology with thicker nanowires indicating core-shell heterostructure; Co₃N shows identical morphology to directly deposited pure Co₃N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Figure 1b) reveals that the MnCo—CH@Co₃N inherits the nanowire array skeleton of MnCo—CH ... A close observation reveals that the morphology of the surface coated Co₃N layers is identical to that of directly deposited pure Co₃N (Figure S1c,d, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals microstructure of Co₃N nanoparticles grown on MnCo—CH and confirms core-shell structure of MnCo—CH@Co₃N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We further employed transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to reveal the microstructure of MnCo—CH@Co₃N. The microstructure of Co₃N nanoparticles grown on the MnCo—CH is shown in Figure S4 (Supporting Information). Additionally, the core-shell structure can be readily identified (Figure 1c)

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice spacing of 0.271 nm corresponds to (221) planes of MnCo-CH; 0.202 nm and 0.214 nm match (101) and (002) planes of Co₃N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacing of 0.271 nm corresponds to the (221) planes of MnCo-CH, whereas 0.202 and 0.214 nm match with the (101) and (002) planes of Co₃N, respectively (Figure 1e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping of MnCo—CH@Co₃N shows Co throughout, N mainly external, Mn mainly inner confirming heterostructure; post-reconstruction shows uniform Mn distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping reveals that the existence of the Co element throughout the whole nanostructure, while the N element exists mainly in the external region and Mn in the inner region (Figure 1g) ... The EDS mapping shows the uniform distribution of Mn throughout the catalyst (Figure 2l)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ Raman shows characteristic Co₃N peaks at 472.1, 514.8, 677.4 cm⁻¹ in MnCo—CH@Co₃N with blue shift vs pure Co₃N indicating electronic interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Though only the characteristic Raman peaks of Co₃N (472.1, 514.8, and 677.4 cm⁻¹) but no MnCo-CH are observed in the MnCo-CH@Co₃N (Figure 1h), possibly due to that the Raman scattering mainly occurs in the dense Co₃N shell. Specially, the blue shift of main peaks in MnCo-CH@Co₃N could be attributed to the strong electronic interaction in the heterostructure.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD reflects co-existence of MnCo-CH and Co₃N bulk phases in MnCo—CH@Co₃N; Co₃N peaks relatively weak due to poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis sensitively reflects the co-existence of MnCo-CH and Co₃N bulk phases (Figure 1i). Compared to pure MnCo-CH sample, the diffraction peaks of Co₃N are relatively weak due to the poor crystallinity and small grains.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS shows Coδ+ (778.1 eV), Co³+ (779.7 eV), Co²+ (782.2 eV) in Co₃N; MnCo—CH@Co₃N shows peak shifts indicating electron transfer from Co₃N to MnCo—CH; barely detectable Mn signals confirm complete Co₃N encapsulation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p XPS spectrum of Co₃N reveals three different Co species (Figure 1j). The main peak at 778.1 eV is ascribed to the Coδ+ ... While in the MnCo-CH@Co₃N, the Coδ+ peak shifts toward higher binding energy regions ... There are barely detectable Mn signals from the surface of the MnCo-CH@Co₃N without etching treatment

nodes.characterization_summary: MnCo—CH@Co₃N has Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 7.42 m² g⁻¹, more than twice that of Co₃N (3.01 m² g⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thanks to the hierarchical structure, the MnCo—CH@Co₃N presents a high Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 7.42 m² g⁻¹, more than twice that of Co₃N (3.01 m² g⁻¹) (Figure S2, Supporting Information).
